newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht weak after rumours, interbank up late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht weak after rumours, interbank up late.

text.p: The Thai baht was under renewed attack by offshore speculators late on Thursday as sluggish economic data released by the central bank added to rumours about a possible baht devaluation, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand promptly denied the rumour, said it was monitoring the market closely and would take necessary measures to defend the currency.
At 1007 GMT, the baht fell to 25.970-25.990 to the dollar, after sliding to as low as 26.00. The baht was traded at 25.915-25.920 in the early morning.
"The rumour emerged in offshore markets after the release of the central bank's key economic data. Some figures were apparently negative," said one dealer at a local bank.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.87, the lowest in 6-1/2 years, against 25.86 on Wednesday.
Dealers said the rising government budget deficit and a high balance of payments deficit for December sparked deep concern about the health of the country's economic fundamentals.
"The baht/dollar trade will remain volatile tomorrow. But most offshore speculators will be cautious to hit the baht on fears the central bank may intervene," another dealer at a foreign bank said.
Dealers said the BOT had made two rounds of intervention today to help stall the baht's slide against the dollar.
Heavy buying of the dollar and rumours of the baht devalution tightened liquidity late on Thursday. Banks were maintaining funds to buy the U.S. unit, dealers said.
